summary: Iteration 3 backend + frontend tested. Backend: 32/32 pytest passed (20 iter-2 regression + 12 new iter-3 tests: MIME validation, GridFS shot endpoint w/ ownership 403 + post-delete 404, rate-limit verification on optimizer/chat, full password-reset flow w/ dev_reset_link, bad/reused/short-token paths, email rate-limit 3/hr). Frontend: /auth show-hide toggle works; forgot-link navigates correctly; /forgot-password dev_reset_link visible; /reset-password toggle + mismatch toast + successful reset + redirect to /auth + login w/ new password verified; no-token state shown when token missing.

minor.issue: TOCTOU race in _rate_limit: count_documents() then insert_one() is not atomic. Concurrent burst of 16 reqs produced only 1 x 429 instead of expected ~6 (race lets requests slip through between count and insert). Manual smoke said ~2; with high concurrency we see fewer 429s. Functionally rate-limit works for normal load.
_rate_limit is awaited BEFORE _validate_and_store_files, so a request with invalid MIME (400) still consumes a deep_dive rate-limit slot. Consider validating MIME first, then rate-limit.

action_items: (Optional) Make rate-limiter atomic — e.g. find_one_and_update with $inc on a per-window doc with TTL, or use Mongo unique-index + ordering. This would tighten the 'optimizer burst -> 2 x 429' guarantee.
(Optional) Reorder MIME check before _rate_limit in create_deep_dive / add_followup so failed validations don't burn a rate-limit slot.

(Optional) The TTL index on db.rate_limits and db.password_resets is referenced in problem statement but not visible in server.py — verify it is being created at startup (otherwise these collections grow unbounded).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~978 lines — should be split into routers (auth, chat, optimizer, deep_dive, password_reset) for maintainability.
_rate_limit has a TOCTOU race; under burst load >limit requests may slip through. Acceptable for current threat model but documented.
Rate-limit + MIME ordering in deep dive create/followup: validate MIME first to avoid burning rate-limit slot on rejected upload.
No explicit TTL index creation in startup code for rate_limits or password_resets collections — these will grow forever without one.
_gridfs_to_b64 loads every file fully into RAM and base64-encodes — fine at 6MB*6 cap but document the upper bound.
